evidence.source: Contract 210 and contract 211 crossed into Production as ONE boundary on 20 August 2026 by guarded rollout run 32359164255 from exact main 1b1be12ba28064ffbb8a5d749b66e0c7925f22f3, gated on encrypted backup 32353845022 and on exact-head rehearsal 32358542321. THIS RECORD IS WRITTEN BY HAND RATHER THAN BY THE FOLLOW-UP AUTOMATION, AND THE REASON MATTERS. A record pull request authored by github-actions[bot] does not trigger this repository's own CI workflows, so its required merge gate never runs and it cannot merge; worse, a superseded automation record drags the committed number BACKWARDS while the database sits ahead. The Production promotion gate reads THIS RECORD AND NOT THE DATABASE, so an under-reported record silently refuses a promotion that is actually safe — which is exactly how the first 209-to-211 rehearsal attempt failed, at the step named 'Refuse to make Production the first hosted environment to see Contract 211'. Development was moved first and Production second, the order the workflows refuse to invert. EVERYTHING BELOW IS AN INDEPENDENT READ-ONLY QUERY AGAINST PRODUCTION taken at 2026-08-20T10:32:54.145874+00, separately from the rollout's own output. THE LEDGER HOLDS 211 ROWS AND NAMES 20260820090000 provider_deadline_watch_tier. THE THREE POLLING TIERS READ AS CONTRACT 211 INTENDS, and on BOTH enabled targets rather than one: sportmonks and football-data each read cadence_minutes 1440, deadline_cadence_minutes 60, deadline_lead_minutes 720, live_cadence_minutes 10, live_lead_minutes 15. That is the whole point of the contract — THE LONG REACH SITS ON THE HOURLY TIER AND THE TEN-MINUTE TIER IS SPENT ONLY ON MATCHES ACTUALLY BEING PLAYED — and it is why the same coverage costs 77 polls a matchweek instead of the 252 measured under contract 210's instrument, against contract 146's published budget of about 58 requests on a matchday. predictor_internal.provider_target_awaits_deadline is installed, and the deadline_lead_minutes column default is 720, so a target created later inherits the watch instead of the gap that caused ING-006. CONTRACT 209 SURVIVES UNDERNEATH: predictor_internal.season_fixture_lifecycle_transitions still holds 0 rows and SportMonks token 10 still resolves to postponed. ZERO TRANSITIONS IS THE REQUIRED OUTCOME AND NOT A DISAPPOINTMENT — a row written during a migration would mean the applier ran at migration time, which it must never do; it runs only from a consumed provider response. NOT ONE PLAYER-OWNED ROW MOVED, every figure matching the Contract-209 record: 1 auth user, 1 profile, 3 entries, 16 season predictions, 36 match predictions, 1 league, 1 league member, 578 season fixtures, 230 ai.bets and 11 cron jobs. THE FIXTURE STATUS HISTOGRAM WAS COMPARED WHOLE RATHER THAN BY TOTAL, because a migration that invented a postponement would leave season_fixtures unchanged at 578 while moving a fixture between statuses; it reads played 12, scheduled 566, before and after. BOTH PUBLICATION GATES REMAIN FALSE and EURO PUBLICATION REMAINS HIDDEN. THIS PROMOTION SPENT NO PROVIDER CREDIT. WHAT IT DOES NOT DO IS MAKE A POSTPONEMENT APPEAR — it makes one findable in time. The deadline watch now opens twelve hours before an unresolved kickoff and polls hourly until it, so a postponement announced inside that window is seen with hours of margin before the lock rather than after it. ING-006 is closed on Production by this record; what remains open is separate and named on the risk register.
